title: Condition Testing and Setting Up the Approximating Model

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(200, 0.8)$. Find the mean and variance of $X$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the mean and the variance of $X$.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(150, 0.6)$. Test whether a normal approximation to $X$ is valid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the conditions $np > 5$ and $nq > 5$ are satisfied.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(40, 0.9)$. Determine whether a normal approximation to $X$ is justified.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate $np$ and $nq$, and state whether a normal approximation is valid.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(120, 0.82)$. Test the validity of a normal approximation.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate $np$ and $nq$ and state your conclusion.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(100, 0.25)$. State the approximating normal distribution $Y$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the distribution $Y \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$ by calculating the mean and variance.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(80, 0.05)$. Check whether a normal approximation to $X$ is valid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate $np$ and $nq$ and state whether the approximation is valid.

questions.text: A fair standard die is thrown 180 times. Let $X$ denote the number of times a six is scored.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why a normal approximation to $X$ is valid.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the approximating normal distribution $Y$, giving its mean and variance.

questions.text: A multiple choice test consists of 60 questions, each with 5 options of which only one is correct. A student guesses every answer independently. Let $X$ be the number of correct answers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Verify that a normal approximation is valid by evaluating $np$ and $nq$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the mean and the exact standard deviation of the approximating normal distribution.

questions.text: In a certain city, 72% of adults use public transport regularly. A random sample of 180 adults is selected. Let $X$ denote the number of adults in the sample who use public transport.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Justify why $X$ can be approximated by a normal distribution.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the mean and variance of the approximating normal distribution, giving the variance to 3 decimal places.

questions.text: A telephone helpline operator connects callers immediately with probability 0.86. In a busy shift, 70 independent calls are received. Let $X$ be the number of calls connected immediately.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Demonstrate that both expected successes and expected failures exceed 5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the approximating normal model $Y \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$, giving $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$ to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: Components manufactured on a production line have a defect rate of 4%. A random sample of $n$ components is inspected.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the smallest integer value of $n$ such that a normal approximation to the number of defective components is valid.

parts.label: b
parts.text: For a sample of size $n = 200$, write down the parameters $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$ of the approximating normal distribution.

questions.text: A rare genetic variation occurs in 2.5% of the population of a species. A researcher samples $n$ individuals at random.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the two conditions required for a normal approximation to the number of individuals with the variation, and determine the least sample size $n$ needed.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that the researcher takes a sample of size $n = 400$, specify the approximating normal distribution $Y \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$ and state its standard deviation $\sigma$ correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the condition $npq > 5$ is not sufficient on its own to justify a normal approximation.

questions.text: An airline knows from long experience that 94% of passengers who book tickets show up for their flight. A flight has 250 bookings. Let $X$ denote the number of passengers who show up.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate $np$ and $nq$, and state with justification whether a normal approximation to $X$ is valid.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the approximating normal model $Y \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$, giving $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$ exactly.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Determine whether a normal approximation would be valid if the flight had only 80 bookings, supporting your answer with calculations.
